# Canonical protocol vectors

## Session requests

The four digest values in `session-requests.tsv` are retained unchanged from
`dragginzgame/ic-auth` commit
`e52a40be75dd9809d0528189d84b43fe96952ad9`, file
`crates/ic-auth/tests/session_request.rs`, tests
`canonical_request_hash_preserves_exact_ttl_choice_and_scope_order` and
`absent_and_explicit_ttl_keep_independent_frozen_hashes`.
Source hashes are recorded in the repository's `reference.sha256`.

The TSV arrangement and surrounding tests are new. Expected values were retained
before implementing the replacement and are not generated by it. Their framing
is the literal ASCII domain `canic-application-session-request-v1` (no NUL),
big-endian u64 scope count, sorted scopes each prefixed by a big-endian u64 byte
length, and a single TTL tag: 0 for absent or 1 followed by big-endian u64 seconds.
The vectors are also checked with Perl `Digest::SHA` using that specification.

These establish unsigned request identity only. They are not signed credential,
Wire, proof-verification, session admission or storage qualification. The
historical domain string is retained for compatibility; there is no Canic
dependency. Original provenance and licensing remain at the repository root.

## Schema-2 claims

`claims-v2.hex` is the exact concatenation of the `VECTOR` string from
`crates/ic-auth/tests/portable.rs` at the same pinned commit. Its decoded length
is 250 bytes and SHA-256 is
`e0d179c866e21b8009fa5dba6bcf85ccc99065f83f141d9e9c2aeb2bc61a2e9d`.
The reference identifies this vector as assembled independently of its Rust
encoder. It was extracted before the replacement codec was written and checked
again using Perl `pack` and `Digest::SHA` against the documented field sequence.
No Python tooling or reference implementation was imported.

The fixture uses Ed25519 tag 1, network/application bytes `11`/`22` repeated
32 times, one-byte issuer/subject `01`/`02`, key/browser bytes `33`/`44`, slot 0,
generation 1, timestamps `0102030405060708`, `1112131415161718`,
`2122232425262728`, `3132333435363738`, nonce `55` repeated 16 times and one
`user` → `read` grant. All multibyte integers are big-endian. Counts and variable
byte lengths are u32; the schema is u16; generation/timestamps are u64. The
domain has its required trailing zero byte. The Certified vector differs only
at mechanism offset 30, where the signed tag is 0.

The deliberately inconsistent time window is accepted by the structural codec;
it cannot pass time validation. These fixtures do not establish proof validity,
browser caller binding, installed Wasm behavior or complete old/new interoperability.
